Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by

MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  JUNE 30, 2020

1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Schmitz, Addleman, Arata, Bayer, Buresh,
  Carman, Carrese, Corman, Medawar,
  Seamans, Shinn, Stegura, Zuckerman

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Silvano

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International
  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International
  Aaron Lobliner, Planner, Michael Baker International
  Dan Wery, Land Use Planner, Michael Baker International

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES,
  JUNE 16, 2020.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
CARMAN to,

  APPROVE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  JUNE 16, 2020.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  COMMERCIAL DISTRICT LAND USE

Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International (MBI), stated that the meeting
tonight will be a commercial district visioning meeting. A few days ago, a five question survey
was sent to the GPAC and great responses and ideas were received; those responses are
included in tonight’s presentation and will be discussed.

Dan Wery, Land Use Planner, Michael Baker International, stated that based on the ideas from
tonght’s meeting, concepts and alternatives will be prepared. A market study and parking study
will be conducted later this summer and all of this will be put together and a draft recommendation
will be prepared.

Mr. Wery provided a summary of the previous discussion on the commercial district including a
summary on public engagement efforts. He also provided a summary on what is affecting change
including: demographics, shopping habits, workplace, mobility and horse ownership.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, JUNE 30, 2020
 Survey Question 1.

What do you think can be done in the Commercial District to help meet the City’s housing needs
based on RHNA allocation of 191 units?

Answers: Mixed-use (6); Higher density housing (4); Affordable senior living (4); Office to high
density residential (2); Mixed income (1); Waive requirement (1); ADUs (1 yes/1 no); Teacher
affordable housing (1); Hotel with residential amenities (1); Density bonuses (1).

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that he would like to discuss marking certain areas,
in particular Town and Country, as off limits to housing. Also, he would like to discuss the vision
for the Promenade property in the event that it is not there in the future.

In response to a question from John Bellas, COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that
mixed-use with retail on the bottom and multi-story residential on top is not really successful from
a neighborhood shopping center standpoint and anything with subterranean parking is not
customer friendly. He also added that he would like to preserve the classic neighborhood
character.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that the Promenade could fill a lot of the housing
needs and can also incorporate commercial and housing. Mixed use would be much more
successful in that part of the Commercial District.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR inquired if any of the existing residential projects can be
used to meet the RHNA allocation of 191 units.

PLANNING MANAGER NAUGHTON stated that none of the existing units can be counted toward
the future RHNA numbers. SB330 prohibits any jurisdictions to lower the allowable density for a
site. Since the Commercial District has a density of 22 units to an acre, the city cannot take away
that right for properties zoned C-3.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR asked how many residential units are completed or currently
under construction. Planning Manager Naughton stated that there are 58 units at 627 Deep
Valley, Drive, 75 units at 927 Deep Valley Drive, 41 restricted senior units at 901 Deep Valley
Drive, 76 assisted living units at Merrill Gardens. Director Wahba added that there are 18 at Silver
Spur Court. Staff confirmed that none of the 268 units can be counted toward RHNA numbers.

Survey Question 2.

What connectivity issues do you think exists in the Commercial District and what do you suggest
to resolve these issues?

Answers: Create unifying elements; Create identity; Mall (obstructs the center, separates retail
centers, inhibits vehicular connection); Issues relating to walking; Increase walkability and
pedestrian connectivity; Provide safe and affordable transportation; Provide online shopping pick-
up accommodations; Park area on top of parking structure; Provide good data service; Co-located
uses to generate synergy; Uses should reflect needs of students; Adapt to online retail; Shared
work spaces; Market/demographic studies; Public transportation, bike lanes and bike parking.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS disagreed with putting a park over a parking structure. She
also asked to discuss redevelopment.

Mr. Wery stated that there has been success in using underutilized parking spaces and creating
community spaces.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CORMAN commented that there is a need for more fields in the city for
youth sports and this is also a way to generate revenue with field rental fees.

Ms. Barbhaya commented that by way of public engagement efforts that MBI is working on, she
has learned that the green spaces at the San Diego Water Front Park are booked for concerts
and this could be a similar destination opportunity for the city. (The San Diego Water Front Park
was used as an example of parking converted to park space)

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN commented that rather than pinpointing items that are
possible, to step back and look at the character of the space and what it could be used for. She
 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, JUNE 30, 2020
 also added to be careful with the height of proposed buildings so that the cliffs which are an
aesthetic feature of the city are not blocked. She also stated the roadside in the center of the
commercial area should be landscaped to draw people through the space.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE commented that, for example the 700 Deep Valley Drive
building and buildings behind that, could be redeveloped and reconfigured to provide parking on
the bottom levels and commercial on the upper levels. She also stated that the renamed street
between Indian Peak and Silver Spur could be reconfigured to allow for a walkway between the
two centers.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA commented that Committee Member Carrese had great
ideas with redeveloping the buildings and also agreed with Committee Member Corman’s idea to
use unused parking space to create green spaces, which would also help the environment.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN reiterated Committee Member Carman’s comments and
stated that the topography of the city should be maintained.

CHAIR SCHMITZ described the type of mobility she would like to see in the Commercial District
without getting in and out of a car. She agrees to look at what the city already has and look at
how mobility and community spaces could be created. If the right policies are put in to place, the
development of the commercial district that we envision could be encouraged.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS stated that in 1974, she got up in a meeting and stated that
the land where the Promenade was being built should be a park and community gathering center
with retail. She expressed her concerned that the needs of the youth of the community has not
been discussed. She also stated that there are several areas between Silver Spur Road and Deep
Valley Drive could be cut-throughs.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR stated that he has been in retail on the Peninsula for 40
years and stated that the biggest challenge is foot traffic and it is really important to solve the
issue by divising better street scape and landscape and connect the shopping centers.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER stated that the Peninsula Center is not a destination and there
is no reason for anyone outside of the city to come there, so it would be nice to have a destination
motiff. She also stated that this is one of the few cities that the residents do not have to pay taxes
since the city has a tax base from the commercial are and this should be kept in mind. She stated
that the connectivity and flow is a huge issue that should be addressed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN suggested that in redeveloping areas, there should be a
requirement to include spaces where people can congregate and provide more people-friendly
spaces.

Survey question 3.

What are the three things you think should be done to create memorable identity and unique
experience in the Commercial District?

Answers: Signature destination; Strong anchor tenant; Peacock alley type shopping; Mini local
history museum; Mall owner (aware of residents desires and purchase ability); Limit building
masses; Modern “main street” feel; Unique experience opportunities; Specific plan on east end.

Mr. Wery provided an example of a plaza with tables, chairs and umbrellas where people gather.
This space was created by closing off a street between two buildings that are mixed-use with
restaurants and retail on the ground floor and residential on top.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS stated that the annual Christmas Parade goes through the
Promenade Mall and and could be set-up much like the plaza example along the parade route.

Mr. Wery provided ideas on events that could bring the community together.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked how enforceable are specific plans. Mr. Wery
stated that the General Plan and Zoning are powerful tools; the Specific Plan is a focused plan
and includes its own zoning. Modified zones could be created to be in line with the specific
character of an area.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  3
 MINUTES, JUNE 30, 2020
 COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ stated that the committee has consensus that the mall is a
space blocking flow and hampering the ability to reconfigure the area; she asked staff what can
be done to change this since the city does not own it. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the
zoning is where the parameters will be set-up for the type of development the city envisions for
the Commercial District. The zoning has to be attractive enough for a developer to want to
redevelop the site. Director Wahba added that the general plan can establish the tools to
incentivise a developer to come in and can provide a “wish list” of what the city desires to have
there; they will want concessions which could include, higher density, higher buildings to provide
open space. The general plan should outline in specific terms what the city wants for the site.

City Manager Grammer stated that as part of the Land Use Element, a Commercial District
focused plan will be prepared, which will look at the balance between residential and non-
residential.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that the focused plan will look at finding what the appropriate
density is for the Commercial District and what the appropriate amount of non-residential is when
residential is proposed. MBI will be preparing a market study and a parking study which will help
inform what the demand is for residential and non-residential.

Mr. Wery stated that what has been seen is the erosion of brick and motar retail space and
repurposing of them. In older areas that are struggling with their commercial spaces, they are
looking to residential to help revive activity. Part of it is finding a balance, design and location.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that the only way to incentivize development will
realistically be through density bonuses and would rather see density in one specific area. He
asked if the residual land value based upon different uses and densities is something that will be
looked at in the economic study. Mr. Wery stated that this is something that will be looked at.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS asked if this is the right time to discuss this. Mr. Wery replied
that it is good to plan and if things change, then adjustments can be made.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA asked about the density and parking studies that are planned
in the future and asked if this is the normal order in the planning process. Mr. Wery stated that
these came up as additional tasks that can be done and stated that it is more helpful to have the
results from these analysis and data. CHAIR SCHMITZ added that some grants have just come
in and this may have shifted the time.

6.  CONSULTANT/STAFF/COMMITTEE ITEMS

Mr. Wery stated that a lot of ideas were discussed encouraged the committee members to submit
any comments that may come up after the meeting. He stated that MBI will consolidate all of this
information and come back with goals, policies and specific recommendations.

CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the committee for completing the survey and for their time and
participation.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested including discussion on rental versus
condominium; and, building types where the construction cost and land cost are greater or equal
to the present value of the future income stream.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that committee members are welcome to submit any comments or
questions between meetings to her or to staff.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 8:03 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved by,

______________________________  _____________________________
Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Velveth Schmitz, Chair

 MINUTES, JUNE 30, 2020
